LESSON: A Dockerfile that COPYs package.json without package-lock.json makes the lockfile decorative for the DEPLOYED artifact: an exact pin in package.json is the only thing standing between a caret range and silent corpus drift in production. Check which file a deploy actually resolves from before trusting a lockfile-based pin.

When a checker's exit code is the gating indicator, a warning-and-exit-0 shape is not a gate. verify-not-specified-classification.mjs had exactly that shape; the fix (exit 1 on a miss) is what makes 'the table covers the population' readable off a pipeline.

A class the interpreter has never been taught throws at write time -- good -- but that means a NEW corpus class is an apply-stopping event, not a warning. Any corpus bump must be accompanied by a table regeneration AND a disposition audit for classes that appear for the first time (AMBIGUOUS_SINGLETON here, 2 rows, would have aborted McLennan).
DEAD-END: A unit test cannot carry the cross-version premise for F3 (the 1.1.0 dist is not installed at 1.4.0). Splitting the claim -- the test pins what the writer does under the pin, the corpora instrument proves the row is new -- was necessary; trying to assert both in one test file was abandoned.

Normalising corpus-dependent strings out of the byte-identical-claim hash was the wrong first instinct; asserting the version and note DIRECTLY and hashing only the job's own logic is what makes the test survive a corpus bump without becoming vacuous.
